use_case: 358 AI Agents Across Woori Bank Operations | Gate News
reported_delivery_components: Samsung SDS deployed 358 AI agents across Woori Bank's operations, the company announced at the Real Summit 2026 conference on the 8th. The implementation spans five core domains: relationship management (RM), corporate credit, wealth management (WM), internal control, and customer service automation. Samsung SDS director Lee Jun-hyung presented the case study titled 'The Beginning of Agentic Bank: Financial Work Innovation Created by AI Agents,' highlighting the deployment as a response to enterprises' difficulty achieving measurable AI outcomes three years after ChatGPT's emergence. The financial sector is accelerating AI transformation to address operational efficiency gaps and standardize service quality across large employee bases.

Samsung SDS implemented 358 AI agents across five operational domains at Woori Bank. The deployment includes approximately 60 agents in RM and corporate credit divisions, and approximately 50 agents in the WM division. The company identified its core challenge as securing completion quality for actual business application rather than determining what to build. Samsung SDS conducted the AI agent construction project for Woori Bank's AI transformation, applying agents to RM, corporate credit, WM, internal control, customer service, and workflow automation.

Samsung SDS applied technology that interprets charts and tables in the RM and corporate credit domains, significantly increasing answer accuracy. When an RM makes requests in natural language, AI proposes corporate analysis reports and customized products. During consultations, the system provides real-time product recommendations based on STT (speech-to-text) technology. In the WM domain, Samsung SDS deployed approximately 50 agents to address sales opportunity losses caused by capability gaps among over 600 private bankers. The company's text-to-SQL technology retrieves accurate data and provides consultation scripts, standardizing private banker capabilities upward. Lee Jun-hyung stated that for corporate AI transformation, work processes must be designed to suit AI from the outset. Samsung SDS plans to actively support financial sector AI transformation based on core project experience and technological capabilities in the financial field, aiming to advance financial company AI from 'AI that asks and answers' to 'AI that works and solves.'
